extensions.note: Token NAMES keep the --pw- prefix and some legacy semantics from a discarded technical-drawing direction (paper, vellum, ink, hair, heavy, notice). The VALUES are all from the current modern-SaaS world. displayName below is the accurate modern name; the key is the CSS variable name minus the leading dashes, so the mapping to EToto.Web/wwwroot/css/etoto.css stays one-to-one.

pw-notice.nameNote: Named 'notice' from the previous world; it is the single action/navigation blue.

brand-blue.nameNote: Power Wave corporate blue. Reserved for the logo and institutional material; it is deliberately NOT an interface token in etoto.css.

pw-warn.nameNote: White text on this fill measures ~4.4:1 — just under the system's own 4.5:1 floor.

pw-idle.nameNote: Same value as pw-ink-3, used as a state fill rather than as text. White text on it measures ~4.4:1 — just under the system's own 4.5:1 floor.

pw-paper.nameNote: Named 'paper' from the previous world; it is the cool blue-grey application background that white cards float on.

pw-sheet.nameNote: The card / bar / field surface. Pure white.

pw-vellum.nameNote: Legacy name; it is the recessed grey wash for pastilles, tags and disabled fields.

pw-vellum-2.nameNote: The faintest wash — hover rows, card and modal footers, info blocks, empty states.

pw-ink-2.nameNote: The stylesheet comment claims 7.6:1; measured on white it is ~7.05:1. Still comfortably AA.

pw-ink-3.nameNote: The stylesheet comment claims 4.9:1; measured on white it is ~4.41:1 and on the Ground ~4.11:1 — below AA for the 13px labels and table headers that use it.

pw-ink-4.nameNote: ~2.3:1 on white. Unavailability signal only; never reading text. Correctly documented as such in the stylesheet.

pw-ink-deep.nameNote: Hover of the dark button only.

pw-hair.nameNote: Legacy name; the default near-invisible divider.

pw-heavy.nameNote: Legacy name; it is still only a 1px hover/focus stroke, not a heavy rule.

display.purpose: The anchor value of an information block — in practice the PLE number. Tabular figures. Drops to 1.5rem below 768px.

title.purpose: h2 (1.125rem) and h3 (1rem); card and modal titles.

body.purpose: The interface default — table cells, paragraphs, buttons, navigation, checkbox labels.

field.purpose: Every text input, select and textarea. Never below 1rem, to stop iOS zoom-on-focus.

label.purpose: Field labels, table headers, info-block keys. Sentence case, no tracking, Ink Muted.

meta.purpose: Top-bar pastille keys, timeline timestamps, balloon numbers.

fontLoading.source: Google Fonts CDN (https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Figtree:wght@400;500;600;700;800&display=swap), preconnected in App.razor
fontLoading.note: One family only. --pw-font-nar is an alias of --pw-font and resolves to the same stack; it is a leftover name from the previous world, not a second face.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: Cards, primary buttons at rest, mobile record cards, the empty-state icon disc.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Hovered primary button. The only hover elevation in the system.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: The login card — a single surface alone on the ground.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Modals only. The largest jump in the system.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Replaces the native outline on :focus-visible everywhere, with 8px radius so it hugs rounded controls.

shadows.name: tabbar-up
shadows.purpose: The fixed bottom tab bar below 768px — the same diffuse language, inverted.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system. Applied to colour, border and shadow transitions.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Buttons, fields, nav items — background, border, colour, shadow.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.value: pw-rise 280ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.3,1) both — opacity 0 to 1, translateY(-4px) to 0
motion.purpose: The state band entering on a record detail (.pw-stamp). The only entrance animation.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) clamps all animation and transition to .001ms and one iteration
motion.purpose: Global escape hatch; it is what keeps the legacy .ple-blink loop from being a hazard.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Information block goes from one column to two.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: The shell switch: at 767.98px and below the nav rail becomes a fixed bottom tab bar and .pw-table-cards collapses tables into record cards.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Information block goes to four columns; card padding and shell gutters relax.

touchTargets.name: tap-lg
touchTargets.purpose: Large buttons and stacked phone actions.

shellMetrics.name: bottom-tabbar
shellMetrics.purpose: Reserved so page content is never hidden behind the phone tab bar.

deadTokens.name: --pw-r-0
deadTokens.note: Defined in etoto.css, referenced nowhere. Nothing in this system is square; treat it as dead, not as permission.

deadTokens.name: --pw-ink-on-dark
deadTokens.note: Defined, used once (pagination active state in Equipamentos). Not a system token.

narrative.overview:
E-toto looks like the tools its users already trust for everything else in their working day. It is a modern light SaaS surface: a soft blue-grey ground, white cards floating on diffuse shadow, generously rounded corners, one humanist sans in sentence case, and a single saturated blue that means *act* or *go here*. The finish bar is explicit and permanent — Monday, Asana, ClickUp — recorded as a brand commitment in PRODUCT.md after the user saw and rejected an authorial technical-drawing direction. Nothing here should read as engineering paper, and nothing should read as a legacy admin theme either.

What keeps it from being generic is that colour is rationed to one job. This is lockout / tagout software: a person reads a screen next to an energised machine and has to know, without hesitating, whether the isolation is active, being released, or finished. So the lockout state is the only thing on the page allowed to wear a saturated red, amber, olive or green, and it wears it as a filled pill with white text — the Monday status pattern — carrying its written label inside. Everything else is grey, and everything actionable is blue. Scanning a list, the eye finds the state column first because nothing competes with it.

Density is comfortable rather than tight: 40px controls, 16px fields, 24px card padding, a 4px-based rhythm. The system is built to survive both scenes the product serves — a long office session on a wide monitor, and a gloved thumb on a phone beside the equipment. Separation between things always comes from elevation and breathing room. Heavy frames, grid lines and coloured card borders are not part of the vocabulary.
keyCharacteristics: White cards floating on a blue-grey ground, 8-20px radius, soft two-layer shadows
Lockout state as a solid colour pill with a written label, never colour alone
Colour has an owner: blue acts, red/amber/green report lockout state, grey does the rest
One typeface (Figtree), sentence case throughout, no tracked capitals
Comfortable touch density: 40/48px targets, 16px fields, 4px spacing rhythm
Phone-first shell: pill nav rail becomes a bottom tab bar, tables become record cards

rules.name: The Colour Has an Owner Rule
rules.body: Blue is action and navigation. Red, amber, olive and green are lockout state, never decoration. Grey is everything else. A new colour needs a new job, and there are no new jobs.

rules.name: The Solid Pill Rule
rules.body: Lockout state renders as a fully filled pill with white text (.pw-sig--*), pill radius, 12px bold. Not a bordered chip, not coloured text, not an icon. Cancelled records are the single exception — .pw-sig--void is a transparent pill with a hairline border and a strikethrough, because the record exists but no longer counts.

rules.name: The Written Label Rule
rules.body: Every state pill contains its label in words. Colour is reinforcement, never the only carrier. A state list gets a .pw-legend strip above it.

rules.name: The Reserved Brand Blue Rule
rules.body: #006CB5 stays on the logo and institutional material. The interface uses #1570DB from the same family. Do not paint UI with the logo blue.

rules.name: The White-Text Floor Rule
rules.body: Every solid state fill is chosen so white text on it clears 4.5:1. Two carried values sit just under the bar — Release Amber (≈4.4:1) and Idle Grey (≈4.4:1) — and should be darkened before the palette is treated as verified; do not add a fifth fill below that line, and do not lower the bar to match them.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: This system has a single typeface. --pw-font-nar exists only as an alias of --pw-font and resolves to the same stack; it is a leftover name, not a second family. Do not introduce a display, condensed or monospace face.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase, no letter-spaced capitals, anywhere. Labels, table headers, buttons, tabs and pills all set text-transform: none and letter-spacing: 0 explicitly, because the framework underneath sets otherwise.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: Text inputs, selects and textareas are 16px and never smaller — including .form-control-sm. Below 16px iOS zooms the page on focus, which is unusable when someone is filling a lockout form one-handed at the machine.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: PLE numbers, timestamps and any figure that appears in a column carry .pw-num (tabular figures, weight 600) so digits line up between rows.

rules.name: The Thumb Rail Rule
rules.body: The navigation is one component with two forms. At 768px and up it is a horizontal strip of pills below the top bar, horizontally scrollable with the scrollbar hidden. Below 768px it detaches, fixes to the bottom of the viewport, spreads its items evenly, stacks icon over 11px label in 54px targets, and pads itself for the home indicator. The page reserves that height (--pw-bottom-h: 62px) so nothing is ever hidden behind it.

rules.name: The Record Card Rule
rules.body: On phone, a table marked .pw-table-cards stops being a table: each row becomes a white record card with its own hairline, 10px radius and soft shadow, and each cell prints its data-label as a 13px muted key at 40% width beside the value. Empty cells disappear. The state cell is ordered first (order: -1), so the lockout state is the first thing read on every card. The header row stays in the DOM, visually hidden.

rules.name: The No Grid Rule
rules.body: Tables have no vertical rules and no filled header. The header is muted 13px text over a single Outline underline; rows are separated by hairlines and distinguished on hover by the Whisper wash. Weight and colour do the work borders would.

rules.name: The Floating Surface Rule
rules.body: Separation comes from elevation and breathing room, never from a heavy frame. A card is a white sheet with a hairline, a 14px radius and the Rest shadow. If two things need to feel distinct, raise one or space them — do not draw a line.

rules.name: The Diffuse Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are wide, soft and low-opacity, tinted with the ink channel. No hard offsets, no dark edges, no coloured glows except the blue focus ring.

rules.name: The Four Steps Rule
rules.body: Rest, Raised, Floating, Lifted — and nothing between. Elevation is a ladder with four rungs, not a continuum.

rules.name: The Nothing Is Square Rule
rules.body: Every container, control and token carries radius. 0 is not an available corner value — a --pw-r-0 token exists in the stylesheet but is referenced nowhere and should be treated as dead, not as permission.

rules.name: The One Selection Mechanism Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one checkbox and one radio in this product: the native input, sized to 18px, tinted with accent-color, sitting in the normal flow with an 8px gap to its label. The icheck-bootstrap and Bootstrap custom-control plugins draw their own boxes on label pseudo-elements; both are switched off with content: none !important. That was not a shortcut — competing with those plugins on specificity failed repeatedly, and re-enabling them will reintroduce the bug where the drawn box loses its tick. Do not restore them, and do not add a third mechanism.

rules.name: The Timeline Echo Rule
rules.body: A timeline dot uses exactly the same colour as the status pill for the same state. The sequence and the status must tell one story.

rules.name: The Neutral Header Rule
rules.body: A modal's intent is expressed by the button in its footer, never by a coloured header. Legacy bg-primary / bg-dark / bg-danger header classes are all forced back to white.

dos: Do float a white card on the blue-grey ground with a 14px radius, a hairline and the Rest shadow. Elevation and space separate things; lines do not.
Do render every lockout state as a solid pill with white text and its written label.
Do keep colour to its owner: blue for action and navigation, the state palette for lockout state only, grey for everything else.
Do set text inputs, selects and textareas at 16px, including small variants.
Do use the native input with accent-color for every checkbox and radio.
Do give tables .pw-table-cards and every cell a data-label, and mark the state cell .pw-cell--state so it leads the record card on phone.
Do keep touch targets at 40px, and 48px for stacked or primary phone actions.
Do put tabular figures (.pw-num) on PLE numbers, timestamps and any column of digits.
Do match a timeline dot's colour to the status pill for the same state.
Do let the state band stick to the top of a long record so the state never scrolls away.
donts: Don't reintroduce square corners, a paper/graphite palette, or technical-drawing typography. This is a permanent brand commitment recorded in PRODUCT.md, not a preference.

Don't set text-transform: uppercase with positive letter-spacing on labels, headers, buttons or tabs. Two page-local styles in Equipamentos and Home still do (.energy-type-text, .template-section-title); they are carried defects, not the pattern.
Don't paint lockout state on a card border, a card header or a modal header. The pill and the tinted band are the only carriers.
Don't add a second typeface. --pw-font-nar is an alias of --pw-font, not a slot.
Don't re-enable the icheck-bootstrap or custom-control drawn boxes. They are disabled deliberately and their pseudo-elements must stay content: none.
Don't use hard-offset, dark-edged or coloured shadows. The only coloured shadow in the system is the blue focus ring.
Don't use Ink Faint for anything a user has to read; it is an unavailability signal.
Don't rely on colour alone for state, and don't ship a state pill without its label.

Don't add infinitely looping animation. .ple-blink (a 1.6s infinite opacity pulse on the maintenance badge) is legacy carried from the previous theme, not a house pattern; it survives only because prefers-reduced-motion clamps it.
Don't introduce a new accent, a new radius step or a fifth elevation. The ladders are closed.
